subject: Recap: Trial environment trade-offs, success criteria & owner commitments
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Nora Patel <nora.patel@medalhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 May 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Trial environment trade-offs, success criteria & owner commitments

Hi Nora —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed path forward so we have a shared checklist to move to a 4-week trial:

Summary of options we discussed (pros/cons, short):
- Hosted Redwood API (fastest): zero infra work, limited to our hosted tenancy; great for functional evaluation and latency profiling; no VPC/workload isolation.
- Dedicated Sandbox (reserved pool): predictable throughput, isolated compute in our fleet; medium setup lead time (1–2 weeks) and more cost but lower ops friction.
- VPC Trial (customer VPC peering / private deployment): full isolation and data residency controls, required network ops and IAM work on your side; lead time typically 2–4 weeks depending on networking approvals.

Proposed success criteria for the POC (we should confirm or edit):
1) Latency SLO: 95th percentile generation latency <= 350ms for 512-token inference under simulated load of 10 qps.
2) Quality: model outputs must exceed your baseline accuracy on the 200-case prompt set (we'll run side-by-side eval).
3) Cost baseline: token cost per 1k tokens within the agreed threshold for the Dedicated option (we'll produce a forecast).
4) Integration: Embedding + semantic search pipeline end-to-end ingest of 50k records within 24 hours.

Owners and immediate asks:
- Nora / Medal Health: confirm data residency requirement (can test on hosted if no legal block) and provide a sample 2k record dataset for embeddings (owner: Aaron).
- Medal IT: if VPC desired, please provide network contact and whether peering or private appliance is preferred.
- Ben Carter (cc): will validate the model variant and produce a draft config for Dedicated vs Hosted, including expected latency/cost. (Ben: can you attach an initial runbook?)
- Marissa Cole (cc): will coordinate eval harness runs and set up monitoring dashboards for the success criteria.

Timeline (proposed):
- Day 0–2: Confirm environment choice and share dataset.
- Day 3–10: Provision hosted trial or dedicate sandbox; if VPC selected, start network approvals (expected 2–4w).
- Week 2: Run baseline eval and latency profiling.
- Week 3–4: Iteration, caching/batching tuning, and final review & success sign-off.

Attachments: trial_scope.xlsx (POC milestones + ask list), poa_connectivity_requirements.md (network checklist).

Next steps (can we lock these by Thursday?):
1) Nora: reply with environment preference (Hosted / Dedicated Sandbox / VPC) and confirm Aaron as dataset owner.
2) Medal IT: share network point-of-contact if VPC.
3) Ben/Marissa: draft technical runbook + evaluation schedule (I asked Ben to attach a preliminary ops note).

If helpful, we can run Hosted for the first 2 weeks to get rapid signal while VPC approvals run in parallel.

Thanks —
Camila Reyes

Subject: Re: Recap: Trial environment trade-offs, success criteria & owner commitments

Camila —

Thanks for the detailed recap, very helpful. A few quick clarifications from our side:

1) Environment preference: we'd like to start Hosted to accelerate the initial eval (agree with testing parallel VPC approval). The goal is to get results within 10 business days.
2) Data residency: our legal team has flagged PHI concerns; for Hosted we can use de-identified/synthetic data for the first two weeks. If initial signals are good we'll prioritize VPC for full-PHI testing.
3) Dataset: Aaron will share a de-identified 2k sample by end of day Wednesday.

Can you confirm that Hosted will let us test the 95th pctl latency target under simulated 10 qps? Also please confirm any limitations on embeddings throughput in Hosted mode.

Finally — cost forecast is important so we can get internal approval. If you can include a ballpark for Hosted vs Dedicated (per-1M tokens and for the dedicated reserve per month) that would be helpful.

Best,
Nora

Nora.Patel@medalhealth.com

Nora —

Quick technical notes on Hosted vs Dedicated vs VPC for the eval goals:

- Hosted: we can absolutely run a 10 qps synthetic load and capture the 95th percentile latency. For the 512-token target, you should expect P95 in the 300–450ms range depending on model variant and concurrency; we'll pick a lower-latency variant for the initial runs. Embedding throughput on Hosted is typically limited by per-account throttles (we'll request a temporary increase for the trial).
- Dedicated Sandbox: predictable P95 < 300ms at similar qps because you get dedicated GPUs and tuned kernels. Startup time to reserve and stage your model/config is ~5–8 business days if we have signed scope.
- VPC: network latency depends on peering/region. If you want sub-300ms P95 we recommend Dedicated in-region; VPC is ideal for PHI but can add 30–90ms for network hops depending on your topology.

Runbook items I'm preparing (attached stub): config.json examples for Dedicated and Hosted, load test script, and a short checklist for VPC peering. If we start Hosted tomorrow I can run the first baseline by Friday EOD.

Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
